rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 20 mm apart across x = -0.04 to +0.04, placed 50 mm ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. The 12 mm footprint is wide enough to see the 25 mm tape from a centred line without saturating. Wheel track 0.12 m and a 0.8 kg mass keep yaw inertia moderate for stable turning. Controller: antisymmetric weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] give a signal that scales with lateral offset. kp=2.5 gives a moderate steering response (about 875 PWM per unit of signal). kd=0.15 damps oscillation without amplifying sensor noise. ki=0 avoids integral windup on curves. base_speed=1.6 gives about 80 percent PWM, which should cover the course in under 3 s (needs about 1.5 m/s average) while leaving headroom for turns. line_loss='last_direction' makes the robot continue in the direction it was last steering when it leaves the tape. Expected result: the baseline completes the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. Measurements requested below will show whether speed or steering gain is the limiting factor.
